title: Hacking Mobile Platforms

objectives.text: List the OWASP Mobile Top 10 2024 risks in order and match a finding (hardcoded key, bad certificate check, IDOR, debug flag) to its category
Recognize smishing, caller ID spoofing, SIM swap / OTP hijacking, juice jacking, overlays and camera or microphone capture, and name the defense for each
Explain the Android security model: UID sandbox with SELinux, permission types, APK signing schemes, Verified Boot and the Keystore
Spot risky Android settings (debuggable, allowBackup, exported components, cleartext traffic, user CAs, network ADB) in a manifest or command output
Explain the iOS security model: secure boot chain, mandatory code signing, sandbox, Data Protection classes, Keychain and ATS
Describe why rooted or jailbroken devices are untrusted, the EC-Council jailbreak types, and how attestation and Lockdown Mode fit in
Compare MDM, MAM, EMM and MTD and choose a deployment model (fully managed, COPE, CYOD, BYOD) and wipe type for a scenario
Use OWASP MASVS/MASTG, NIST SP 800-124r2 and 800-163r1, MITRE ATT&CK Mobile and CISA guidance, and name the common mobile testing tools

readingMap.why: The OWASP Mobile Top 10 2024 order and the SMS/OTP/spoofing attacks are frequent scenario questions.
Sandbox, permissions, rooting, ADB and manifest settings carry most of the Android questions; learn the concepts, skip tool screenshots.
Know the jailbreak types and the iOS protections by name; the exploit details are not needed.
MDM vs MAM, BYOD vs COPE and remote wipe choices are classic scenario questions.
Learn what each tool does in one line and the main guideline names; skip vendor product lists.

labs.name: Analyze an OWASP MAS reference app with MobSF
labs.skill: Reading a static analysis report: manifest flags, hardcoded secrets, network settings, mapped to MASVS

labs.name: Solve a beginner MAS crackme in the Android emulator
labs.skill: Decompiling a practice app with jadx and apktool to see why client-side checks and hardcoded secrets fail

labs.name: Harden your own Android phone and review its app permissions
labs.skill: Play Protect, updates, unknown-sources settings, runtime permissions and developer options, as a user and as an MDM would

labs.name: Map a mobile malware report to ATT&CK for Mobile in the Navigator
labs.skill: Turning a mobile threat write-up into tactics, techniques and mitigations (attestation, enterprise policy)

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a friend why a text message code is a weak second factor, what a SIM swap is, and what she should use instead.
Compare how Android and iOS stop one app from reading another app's data, and explain what rooting or jailbreaking changes for a company's security team.
A small company wants staff to read work email on their own phones. Explain the choices (MDM, MAM, work profile, selective wipe) and which one you would recommend.
